sports.h3: Alcaraz and Sabalenka cruise into US Open third round
sports.summary: Both defending champions cleared rain-delayed second round matches in New York on Wednesday, with Sabalenka needing just 53 minutes and Alcaraz recovering from a lost first set.
body: Carlos Alcaraz, playing his first tournament since a wrist injury sidelined him in April, dropped the opening set to Portugal's Jaime Faria before taking control and winning 4-6, 6-0, 6-3, 6-2. The second seed is the clear favourite in the men's draw after world number one Jannik Sinner withdrew before the tournament with a right knee injury and Novak Djokovic lost in the first round to Mariano Navone.

Aryna Sabalenka was even more efficient. The top seed beat 160th-ranked Russian qualifier Polina Iatcenko 6-1, 6-1 in 53 minutes as she chases a rare third consecutive US Open title. Ben Shelton also advanced with a 6-3, 5-7, 7-6(3), 7-5 win over Hubert Hurkacz, while Frances Tiafoe, Jessica Pegula and Karolina Muchova joined him in the third round.

The 2026 edition runs until 13 September, with the women's semifinals on 10 September and finals weekend on 12-13 September. Rain disrupted the Wednesday schedule, forcing matches onto the two stadium courts with roofs.

sports.h3: Musetti and Auger-Aliassime crash out as Fritz, Osaka and Swiatek roll on
sports.summary: Day five at Flushing Meadows brought two surprise exits in the men's draw while the leading women advanced without fuss.
body: Australian Dane Sweeny produced the upset of Thursday, beating Lorenzo Musetti 3-6, 6-1, 6-2, 6-2 in the second round. Felix Auger-Aliassime also departed, losing 6-7, 6-3, 6-2, 6-2 to Karen Khachanov.

Taylor Fritz needed only three quick sets to dispatch Mattia Bellucci 6-0, 6-1, 6-1. On the women's side Iga Swiatek beat Nadia Podoroska 6-3, 6-2, and Naomi Osaka and Madison Keys also moved into the third round. Coco Gauff and Alexander Zverev were scheduled for the later session.

sports.h3: Pegula says influencer circus at US Open is going too far
sports.summary: The American star complained that ring lights and flash photography from content creators are becoming a distraction, while Medvedev sees more upside than downside.
body: Jessica Pegula told reporters in New York that influencer behaviour at this year's tournament is starting to become a little too much, citing ring lights and flashes going off during play. The USTA has been courting creators to reach younger audiences, and their presence on the grounds has grown sharply.

Daniil Medvedev took a more relaxed view, saying the extra attention had brought more benefits than problems for the sport. Reuters reported that the boom is testing the boundaries of traditional tennis etiquette, with players and umpires now dealing with distractions that did not exist a few years ago.

sports.h3: SailGP makes its Valencia debut this weekend
sports.summary: The inaugural Spain Sail Grand Prix runs 5-6 September, with home team Los Gallos arriving second in the standings and 14 points off the lead.
body: Valencia hosts SailGP for the first time on Saturday and Sunday, with fleet racing on Saturday and the finals on Sunday. The city has a deal to stage the Spanish round through 2028 after the event was moved from its previous Spanish venue.

Spain's team, nicknamed Los Gallos and led by Olympic champions Diego Botin and Florian Trittel, comes into its home event sitting second in the 2026 championship, 14 points behind the leader. The F50 foiling catamarans race close to the shore, so spectators can follow the action from the marina.

sports.h3: Team USA joins the fleet for America's Cup regatta in Naples
sports.summary: The second preliminary regatta of the 38th America's Cup takes place 24-27 September on the 2027 race course, with six teams and nine AC40s lining up.
body: Emirates Team New Zealand says the Naples event will be the first competitive racing on the waters that will decide the next America's Cup. Teams sail identical AC40 foiling yachts, using the regatta to test crew combinations and learn the local conditions.

American Racing Challenger Team USA joins the preliminary fleet for the first time this cycle, while the Australian entry will not yet take part. That leaves six teams and nine boats on the Bay of Naples.

sports.h3: Hamilton arrives at Monza in an F40 and backs Ferrari to win
sports.summary: Ferrari brings an upgraded engine to its home race this weekend, and Lewis Hamilton says he strongly believes the team can take victory on Sunday.
body: Hamilton set the tone on Thursday by turning up outside the paddock gates in a classic Ferrari F40 he recently bought, then told the FIA press conference that being a Ferrari driver at Monza is the best feeling in the sport. He shares Group 1 of the press conference with Oliver Bearman and Pierre Gasly.

Ferrari has an upgraded power unit ready and has been weighing whether to deploy it at Monza, where a home win would carry enormous weight for the team. The 2026 cars, with their new power units and rear tyres, are expected to be roughly two seconds a lap quicker than last year around the 5.793 km circuit, and slipstream tactics dominated paddock talk on Thursday.

sports.h3: Championship leader Antonelli starts his home race from the back
sports.summary: Mercedes is fitting a completely new power unit to Kimi Antonelli's car at Monza, sending the 20-year-old to the rear of the grid whatever he does in qualifying.
body: Twelve races into the season, Antonelli has already used the maximum allocation of four of the seven power unit components, including his fourth engine and exhaust and his third energy store and control electronics. After a string of reliability problems, including a retirement in Barcelona, Mercedes decided a full fresh unit was the safer option.

Toto Wolff said the team's calculations showed Monza was the best place to take the hit, since the long straights give plenty of overtaking chances. Antonelli says he has nothing to lose and will go full attack in front of his home crowd.

sports.h3: Ajax lands Kehrer and Adingra as Dutch window slams shut
sports.summary: Deadline day brought 11th and final summer signings for Ajax, while PSV re-signed Sam Lammers and Feyenoord brought back Reiss Nelson.
body: Ajax finished a busy window by taking German international defender Thilo Kehrer on a one-year loan from AS Monaco and winger Simon Adingra on loan from Sunderland. The Amsterdam club ends the summer with 11 new arrivals.

Champions PSV brought former striker Sam Lammers back to Eindhoven and also secured a 17-year-old talent, while Feyenoord reunited with winger Reiss Nelson. Across Europe clubs spent a record amount, with Martinelli's move to Al-Hilal among the day's biggest deals, and World Cup player Iqbal left FC Utrecht.

sports.h3: Ajax host PSV on Saturday in first topper of the season
sports.summary: Matchday 5 brings the champions to the Johan Cruijff ArenA at 20:00, with Feyenoord travelling to NEC earlier in the afternoon.
body: The Eredivisie schedule put the first meeting of Ajax and reigning champions PSV as early as the fifth round. Kick-off in Amsterdam is Saturday 5 September at 20:00, and Ajax will be able to field new loan signings Kehrer and Adingra.

Feyenoord play NEC Nijmegen in Nijmegen at 16:30 the same afternoon after a stumble in the previous round, while FC Utrecht host Go Ahead Eagles at 18:45 and Willem II meet Excelsior at 21:00. Sunday's programme includes Groningen against Twente, Heerenveen against AZ and ADO Den Haag against Fortuna Sittard.

sports.h3: Feyenoord agree improved deal to keep Zechiel
sports.summary: The 22-year-old midfielder turned down interest from Lille and Villarreal and will sign an upgraded contract in Rotterdam.
body: Feyenoord have reached a verbal agreement with Gjivai Zechiel on reopening and improving his contract, according to reports on Thursday. His current deal runs to mid-2028 but will be rewritten with a substantial pay rise.

Zechiel attracted concrete interest this summer, with Lille presenting several proposals and Villarreal also monitoring him. Feyenoord rejected the French approaches, treating the midfielder as a player they wanted to keep at any cost.

sports.h3: ADCC 2026 locks in 104 athletes for Krakow
sports.summary: The no-gi world championship on 12-13 September will crown a new superfight champion after Gordon Ryan's retirement, with Kaynan Duarte facing Yuri Simoes.
body: ADCC has confirmed its complete lineup of 104 competitors for the World Championship at Tauron Arena in Krakow, the first time Poland hosts the event. The men's divisions at 66, 77, 88, 99 and +99 kg are 16-athlete brackets, while the women's 55, 65 and +65 kg divisions have eight athletes each.

With Gordon Ryan retired in early 2026 and the superfight belt vacant for the first time in 17 years, the headline bout pairs the two most recent absolute champions, Kaynan Duarte and Yuri Simoes. Three previous ADCC champions are not on the card and Mica Galvao's status has been a talking point.

sports.h3: IBJJF World Master under way in Las Vegas
sports.summary: The three-day championship for over-30 competitors runs 3-5 September at the Las Vegas Convention Center alongside Jiu Jitsu Con.
body: The IBJJF World Master Championship opened on Thursday in halls W1 to W3 of the Las Vegas Convention Center and runs through Saturday. It is one of the largest gi tournaments on the calendar, with divisions from Master 1 through the oldest age brackets.
Running in parallel, Jiu Jitsu Con brings seminars from BJJ legends and industry panels for thousands of fans. All mats stream live on FloGrappling and the FloSports app.

sports.h3: Omrzel, 20, wins Vuelta stage 12 as Mas tightens grip on red
sports.summary: The Slovenian became the youngest Grand Tour stage winner since 1981 on Calar Alto, while Enric Mas attacked to extend his lead over Primoz Roglic to 1:45.
body: Jakob Omrzel won the 166.5 km mountain stage from Vera to the Calar Alto observatory on Thursday, beating Urko Berrade and Santiago Buitrago. At 20 years, 5 months and 13 days he is the youngest Slovenian to win a Grand Tour stage and the youngest Grand Tour stage winner since Celestino Prieto at the 1981 Vuelta.

Behind him, race leader Enric Mas went on the attack on the final climb and gained close to 30 seconds on Primoz Roglic, his nearest rival. Roglic remains second overall, 1:45 behind the Movistar rider.

consumer-tech.h3: Xiaomi storms IFA with 380 products and a 2027 European car launch
consumer-tech.summary: The Chinese company made its Berlin debut on 3 September, unveiled its Mijia smart home brand for Europe and signed eight German dealer groups to sell its EVs from 2027.
body: Xiaomi used its first ever IFA stand to show more than 380 products across phones, smart home gear, computing, robotics and cars, built around what it calls a Human x Car x Home strategy. The Mijia ecosystem brand is getting a large-scale European rollout for the first time.

The biggest news came from Xiaomi Auto, which signed memoranda of understanding with eight German dealer groups and confirmed Germany as its first European market in 2027. That points to a dealer model rather than Tesla-style direct sales. The company has sold about 700,000 cars in China and brought its SU7 and YU7 models plus a Vision Gran Turismo concept to Berlin.

IFA 2026 opens to the public on 4 September and runs to 8 September. Chinese exhibitors dominate the show this year with 932 companies, and organisers say they account for nearly 85 percent of the robots on display.

consumer-tech.h3: Samsung leaves the IFA show floor, brings a 1,100Hz monitor instead
consumer-tech.summary: For the first time in 35 years Samsung is not on the Messe Berlin floor, showing its lineup at Humboldt Carre in central Berlin as the Galaxy S26 FE goes on sale.
body: Samsung swapped its 93,600 square foot trade show booth for a business-focused showcase called Samsung Connect in the centre of the city. The move ends a run at Messe Berlin that dated back to 1991.

The star of the display lineup is the Odyssey G6 G60H, a 27-inch Fast IPS monitor that reaches 1,100Hz at HD resolution and 600Hz at its native 2560 x 1440. It supports HDR10+, FreeSync Premium and G-Sync and launches globally late this year, alongside four new Odyssey OLEDs topped by a 49-inch 1,300-nit flagship.

consumer-tech.h3: Dyson unveils ten products including a 499 dollar camera toothbrush
consumer-tech.summary: The CameraJet uses a macro lens and machine learning to find gaps between teeth and floss them while you brush, part of Dyson's push into AI and robotics.
body: At its Unveiled event in Berlin on Thursday, Dyson showed ten new products spanning floor care, air purification, hair care, robotics and, for the first time, oral care. The company frames the range as a shift from purely mechanical devices toward machines that can see and respond to their surroundings.

The CameraJet toothbrush carries a 100-kilopixel macro lens that captures 28 images a second and uses what Dyson calls Gap Optical Targeting to direct a water jet between teeth. It is priced at 499 dollars and listed as coming soon.

consumer-tech.h3: Nvidia RTX Spark PCs with 1 petaflop of local AI land in October
consumer-tech.summary: Acer, Asus and Lenovo showed the first Windows machines built on Nvidia's Grace CPU and Blackwell GPU platform at IFA, with 128GB of unified memory at the top end.
body: Nvidia confirmed at IFA that RTX Spark desktops and thin-and-light laptops from more than half a dozen partners will ship in the coming weeks, with systems starting to reach the market in October. The platform pairs up to a 20-core Grace CPU with a 6,144-core Blackwell RTX GPU and up to 128GB of unified memory.

Lenovo announced the Yoga Pro 9n and the Yoga 9n 2-in-1 on the platform, Asus showed ProArt P16 and P14 laptops plus a GR1X desktop, and Acer displayed a compact desktop concept. Nvidia also introduced PAIR, a home-focused framework for one-click AI agents that run locally.

consumer-tech.h3: Apple's 'Surprise and shine' event is next Wednesday
consumer-tech.summary: The 9 September keynote at Apple Park is expected to bring the iPhone 18 Pro, 18 Pro Max and a foldable that may be called iPhone Ultra, with no base iPhone 18 until spring.
body: Apple sent invitations on 26 August for a 9 September event starting at 10:00 Pacific, 19:00 in the Netherlands. The tagline is Surprise and shine and the stream will run on YouTube and Apple's own channels.

Reporting from MacRumors and AppleInsider points to a split launch cycle this year: the Pro models and the first foldable in September, with the standard iPhone 18 held back until spring 2027. iOS 27, unveiled at WWDC in June, is expected to ship later this month with a redesigned Apple Pay checkout, Mail fixes and Siri AI limited to newer iPhones.

consumer-tech.h3: Switch 2 price rises to 499 dollars as a stacked September begins
consumer-tech.summary: Nintendo's console now costs 50 dollars more in the US, just as Onimusha, NBA 2K27, Fire Emblem and a native Witcher 3 remaster head to the platform.
body: Nintendo's previously announced US price increase from 449.99 to 499.99 dollars took effect on 1 September. Orbitals, a co-op sci-fi adventure with an 80s anime look, launched on 3 September.

The release calendar is dense: NBA 2K27 and Onimusha: Way of the Sword on 4 September, Valheim on 9 September and Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave on 17 September, alongside Wo Long, LEGO Batman, Dragon Quest, Minecraft Dungeons II and a native remaster of The Witcher 3 later in the month. Game Rant counts eight big Switch 2 releases in September, two of them exclusives.

consumer-tech.h3: Tesla launches the Cybercab in Austin with no wheel and no pedals
consumer-tech.summary: Thursday evening's invite-only event put members of the public in the two-seat robotaxi on public roads for the first time, with Musk promising a storm of Cybercabs.
body: Tesla held its Cybercab launch at its Austin headquarters on 3 September, livestreamed and attended by selected Robotaxi riders and sweepstakes winners aged 21 and over. The gold two-seater has butterfly doors, no steering wheel or pedals and relies on Tesla's AI4 computer and cameras. Production started at Gigafactory Texas in the first half of 2026.

Texas DMV records show Tesla added 38 Cybercabs to its commercial fleet ahead of the event, taking the total to 45, and a Robotaxi app update already supports Cybercab rides in Austin. Morgan Stanley's bull case sees unsupervised paid rides across Austin and Houston, while Reuters and TechCrunch flagged open questions about regulatory approval and how large the initial service area will be.

consumer-tech.h3: Ford targets 100,000 Fathoms in year one of its 28,350 dollar pickup
consumer-tech.summary: Only Tesla has ever hit that first-year number with a single EV in the US. Pre-orders open early 2027 with deliveries later that year.
body: Ford wants the Fathom, its affordable electric pickup, to become an instant best-seller with 100,000 units in its first model year. Carscoops notes that no individual EV other than a Tesla has managed that in America.

The truck starts at 28,350 dollars before a 1,595 dollar destination fee, keeping Ford's promise of a sub-30,000 dollar price. The base model gets a standard-range battery rated around 300 miles, more passenger space than a Toyota RAV4, BlueCruise-ready hardware, a digital key and bidirectional charging as standard.

consumer-tech.h3: EVs outsold petrol cars in Australia for the first time in August
consumer-tech.summary: Battery-electric vehicles took 24.9 percent of the Australian market, every top seller built in China, while UK BEVs outsold every other powertrain the same month.
body: August 2026 was the first month in which battery-electric cars beat petrol cars in Australian sales, with a 24.9 percent share. Electrek notes that every one of the best-selling EVs in the country is manufactured in China.

In the UK, battery-electric cars outsold every other powertrain in August, yet the government is under pressure to soften its zero-emission vehicle targets. Across 16 major European markets BEVs reached 25.7 percent of registrations in July, after a 20.7 percent EU share in the first half.

consumer-tech.h3: Largest EV battery study ranks which models age best
consumer-tech.summary: Aviloo analysed roughly 500,000 battery health checks across 20 popular EVs and found Tesla's nickel packs middling, with LFP packs and one Hyundai model standing out.
body: Austrian diagnostics firm Aviloo published results from what it calls the largest EV battery health study to date, covering around 500,000 checks on 20 common models. The data shows wide differences in how much capacity cars retain after similar mileage.

Tesla's nickel-based Model 3 packs earned only a middling grade, which cuts against the reputation the brand has built on battery durability, although Aviloo's newer data has been kinder to Tesla's LFP packs. InsideEVs reports that one Hyundai model stood out for retention.

consumer-tech.h3: Rivian spin-off ALSO delays its TM-B e-bike yet again
consumer-tech.summary: Launch Edition reservation holders are now told to expect delivery by early November, after a spring launch slipped to mid-September last month.
body: ALSO, the micromobility company spun out of Rivian, sent customers a new update saying Launch Edition TM-B bikes are now shipping and will arrive in waves between now and early November. The bike was unveiled last October with a spring 2026 target.

The company blames stress on global supply chains and a spike in demand for raw materials and electronic components. Some reservation holders on social media are questioning whether bikes have reached ordinary customers rather than influencers and people connected to the company, and some began cancelling orders over the summer.

consumer-tech.h3: Windows 11 lets you move the taskbar again from 8 September
consumer-tech.summary: Update KB5120998 reverses one of Windows 11's most criticised design decisions and adds a resizable Start menu and a switch to disable web results in Search.
body: Microsoft's September update, KB5120998 for builds 26200.9278 and 26100.9278, rolls out on 8 September to Windows 11 24H2 and 25H2. A new Taskbar position setting under Personalization allows Bottom, Top, Left or Right, restoring flexibility that Windows 10 users lost almost five years ago.

The same release adds a resizable Start menu and a privacy control that turns off web results in Windows Search. PCMag describes the taskbar change as Microsoft finally backing down after years of user requests; the company first promised it in February.

consumer-tech.h3: ChatGPT adds sticker packs, pronunciation and iMessage access on Mac
consumer-tech.summary: OpenAI's latest consumer updates turn prompts or photos into shareable stickers and let the Mac app read and send Messages conversations.
body: OpenAI's release notes for early September list a mobile feature that turns an idea or a photo into a set of stickers for sharing in iMessage and WhatsApp, plus tap-to-hear pronunciation with phonetic breakdowns for words and phrases.

On Apple silicon Macs, an Apple Messages plugin for the ChatGPT desktop app can now read and search iMessage, SMS and RCS threads and prepare or send messages. Plus and Pro subscribers can also change the hosted URL of a ChatGPT Site without redeploying it.

consumer-tech.h3: iOS 27 overhauls Apple Pay checkout and fixes long-standing Mail bugs
consumer-tech.summary: Days before release, 9to5Mac details a rebuilt Apple Pay flow, while Macworld shows the update actually speeds up older iPhones.
body: iOS 27, first shown at WWDC in June, is expected to reach iPhones later this month after the 9 September event. 9to5Mac calls the redesigned Apple Pay checkout the service's best upgrade in years, and lists three Apple Mail fixes that longtime users have been waiting for.

Macworld's testing found that older iPhones get faster with the update even though the new Siri AI features are limited to newer hardware. CNET says Safari on iOS 27 reverses the most annoying change from iOS 26.
